profile.persona_definition: The user is an AI researcher heavily focused on computational efficiency, token reduction, and long-context processing in Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Their primary interest lies in the intersection of context compression, efficient reasoning (e.g., accelerating Chain-of-Thought or RL training), and information-theoretic approaches to language modeling (e.g., entropy estimation, sparse attention, information bottlenecks). They seek foundational architectural and algorithmic improvements that reduce the quadratic cost of attention and long-tail generation without sacrificing model capabilities.
negative_constraints: Lower priority unless focusing on core LLM token efficiency: Robotics, autonomous driving, and embodied AI/GUI agents.
Lower priority unless demonstrating novel token compression: Pure video understanding tasks, text-to-image/video generation, and segmentation.
Lower priority: Hardware-level memory management or traditional systems optimization (e.g., DLRM inference buffers) that do not innovate at the algorithmic/token level.
ranking_heuristics: Prioritize papers explicitly addressing 'context compression', 'token reduction', 'sparse attention', or 'gist tokens'.
Elevate research that improves the efficiency of reasoning models, such as compressing Chain-of-Thought (CoT) paths, accelerating RL rollouts, or mitigating long-tail generation costs.
Favor principled, information-theoretic approaches to language modeling, such as using entropy estimation, predictability, or semantic boundaries to guide compression and generalization.
Highly rank major foundational model releases (e.g., DeepSeek-V3.x) that introduce significant architectural breakthroughs in context scaling or training efficiency.

When evaluating multimodal/retrieval papers, look for 'extreme compression' or dense representation techniques (e.g., token fusion, minimal vectors per page) rather than standard RAG or embedding applications.
